answer: One defence is a warehouse-lot binding rule. Each seat must own a named lot of saffron drying on one island, plus a sealed sampling tube in that loft. Each epoch it files the lot's gas chromatogram, the loft temperature log and the zephyr direction at the shutters. The safranal-to-crocetin ratio drifts with humidity, turning schedule and sea air, so no spectrum can be pre-computed or replayed. Two seats on one lot yield near-identical spectra and both lose their bonds. A sybil farmer needs one real lot, one tube and one lab run per identity, paying in inventory that extra keys cannot fake.
